solution.shortcut: Know the positions by heart through EJOTY (E 5, J 10, O 15, T 20, Y 25); a reverse position is 27 minus the forward one.
solution.trap: '192' comes from using reverse positions.

items.prompt: In a certain code language, 'BEAD' is written as '25222623'. How will 'FISH' be written in that code language?

steps: Rule: Each letter is written as its position from the end of the alphabet (A = 26 … Z = 1), and the numbers are written side by side.
Written side by side: '2118819'.
solution.shortcut: Know the positions by heart through EJOTY (E 5, J 10, O 15, T 20, Y 25); a reverse position is 27 minus the forward one.
solution.trap: '1981821' comes from writing the numbers in reverse order.

items.prompt: In a certain code language, 'TIGER' is written as '157' and 'MONKEY' is written as '164'. How will 'ZEBRA' be written in that code language?

steps: Rule: 2 × the sum of the letters' reverse positions (A = 26 … Z = 1) + (number of letters).
solution.shortcut: Know the positions by heart through EJOTY (E 5, J 10, O 15, T 20, Y 25); a reverse position is 27 minus the forward one.
solution.trap: '109' comes from using forward positions.

items.prompt: If the letters of the word 'FIGHTER' are arranged in alphabetical order from left to right, how many letters will remain at the same position?

steps: Letters with positions: F(1) I(2) G(3) H(4) T(5) E(6) R(7).
Arranged in alphabetical order: E F G H I R T.
Compare position by position: F/E, I/F, G/G ✓, H/H ✓, T/I, E/R, R/T.
Unchanged: G (3), H (4) → 2 letters.
solution.shortcut: Write the arranged letters directly under the word and tick matches — no need to rewrite the whole word twice.
solution.trap: Count only letters in exactly the same position — a letter that merely moves one place does not count.

items.prompt: If the letters of the word 'CRIMSON' are arranged in reverse alphabetical order from left to right, how many letters will remain at the same position?

steps: Letters with positions: C(1) R(2) I(3) M(4) S(5) O(6) N(7).
Arranged in reverse alphabetical order: S R O N M I C.
Compare position by position: C/S, R/R ✓, I/O, M/N, S/M, O/I, N/C.
Unchanged: R (2) → 1 letter.
solution.shortcut: Write the arranged letters directly under the word and tick matches — no need to rewrite the whole word twice.
solution.trap: Arranging A → Z instead of Z → A is the usual slip; read the direction carefully.

items.prompt: In the word 'HARVEST', each vowel is replaced by the next letter and each consonant by the previous letter of the English alphabet. If the new letters are then arranged in alphabetical order from left to right, how many letters will remain at the same position?

steps: Change the letters: H→G, A→B, R→Q, V→U, E→F, S→R, T→S → GBQUFRS.
Arranged in alphabetical order: B F G Q R S U.
Compare position by position: G/B, B/F, Q/G, U/Q, F/R, R/S, S/U.
No letter stays in place → none.
solution.shortcut: Write the arranged letters directly under the word and tick matches — no need to rewrite the whole word twice.
solution.trap: Change the letters first; comparing the original word with the sorted new letters gives a wrong count.

items.prompt: If the first four letters of the word 'TOWNSHIP' are arranged in alphabetical order and the last four letters in reverse alphabetical order (each group staying in its own half), how many letters will remain at the same position?

steps: Letters with positions: T(1) O(2) W(3) N(4) S(5) H(6) I(7) P(8).
First half TOWN in alphabetical order: N O T W; second half SHIP in reverse alphabetical order: S P I H.
Compare position by position: T/N, O/O ✓, W/T, N/W, S/S ✓, H/P, I/I ✓, P/H.
Unchanged: O (2), S (5), I (7) → 3 letters.
solution.shortcut: Write the arranged letters directly under the word and tick matches — no need to rewrite the whole word twice.
solution.trap: Sort each half separately — sorting all eight letters together, or both halves the same way, changes the count.
